A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–H. Retained material can be matched reliably despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of linear-network training, including comparisons with DMFT predictions, learning-rate sweeps, and experiments on power-law data.

after.justification: v3 retains these simulations and adds power-law learning-rate transfer results and early online-SGD dynamics experiments in Figures 7 and 9.

M1.justification: v3 corrects the stated output normalization by adding a sqrt(D) prefactor in Eqs. 1, 16, 22 and Appendix F, aligning these definitions with v1's existing error-vector derivation. This is a limited model-specification correction; the architectures, squared-loss objective and GD/SGD procedures are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic regression with isotropic Gaussian and structured power-law features. The added experiments remain within this coverage; unequal widths and multiple outputs were already theoretical extensions in Appendices F and G.

E2.justification: The evaluated contrasts between NTK and mean-field/muP parameterizations, and between unscaled and depth-scaled residual networks, are retained. The new power-law transfer experiment uses the existing NTK-versus-muP comparison; newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds a power-law learning-rate sweep using L=3 and batch size B=128 (Figure 7), plus checks of the first ten SGD steps across width and batch-size ratios (Figure 9). These are additional experimental settings, rather than reported revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 and Figure 9 test an approximation explaining the initial loss increase already visible in v1's Figure 3. Figure 7 additionally examines whether learning-rate transfer persists with power-law features, extending the existing sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added figures do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original plotted results are retained unchanged. New Figure 7 reports approximately aligned muP learning-rate optima and shifting NTK optima on power-law data; Figure 9 adds simulated early-loss trajectories and approximate predictions across width and batch-size ratios.

T1.justification: v3 expands Appendix C with explicit finite- and infinite-depth residual correlation and loss-closure equations, and adds an early-SGD loss recurrence and instability threshold in Appendix D.2 (Eqs. 103–105). It also corrects duplicated factors in Eq. 65. Appendix D.1 primarily consolidates the previously specified online-SGD equations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and concluding discussion retain the same central claims: DMFT characterization of training, width/depth hyperparameter transfer, and accelerated power-law learning on hard tasks. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly warns that the accelerated scaling law is a gradient-flow result that long-run discrete-time edge-of-stability effects may invalidate. Appendix D.2 also links early loss growth to learning rate, depth, width and batch size, extending the interpretation of an existing observation.

D1.justification: Figure 7 documents the added experiment's configuration: L=3, B=128, power-law exponents (2, 1.75), gamma_0=0.4, and widths 16–1024. No code-access or hardware information is added, and Table 1's computational-cost estimates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Bayesian kernel-renormalization research by Pacelli, Baglioni, Aiudi and Bassetti and colleagues. Cohen et al. and Ren et al. are added for the discrete-time stability qualification. The overall novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 adds focused explanatory passages, Appendix D.1–D.2 subsections and an impact statement, labels the two training settings explicitly, and repairs the unresolved appendix reference in Section 2. Most prose and the main section/appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds two two-panel figures, numbered 7 and 9. v1's Figures 7 and 8 become Figures 8 and 10 without changes to their plots; Table 1 moves to a separate final page. Existing displays retain their overall design.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for transfer on structured data, expands the analytical treatment and states a meaningful discrete-time limitation absent from v1. These improve an otherwise stable paper, although Eq. 104 and Figure 9's caption give inconsistent early-growth coefficients, limiting confidence in that new analysis.
